segment: Chat-speed MoE serving at a fixed power budget
rationale: The largest and fastest-growing inference pool, but NVL72 serves ~2.6M tokens/s per MW vs <=0.7M for shipping rivals (Est.) and Rubin roughly doubles it
notes: Repo judgement; tokens per MW from the chapter 14 model at 50 tokens/s per user

segment: Capacity-bound serving (large models at low batch; long-context KV cache)
rationale: LPDDR costs an implied ~$20/GB vs ~$53/GB forecast for HBM4 and needs no CoWoS; NVIDIA answers with 54 TB of CPU-side LPDDR5X per Vera Rubin rack and 1 TB HBM4E on Rubin Ultra
notes: Implied LPDDR price = ~$1.1M SOCAMM / 54 TB (repo calc from Morgan Stanley figures)

segment: High-interactivity premium decode (>=100 tokens/s per user)
rationale: Per-user speed is capped by bandwidth per weight read; SRAM designs lead and NVIDIA now sells Groq 3 LPX racks for this tier
notes: LPDDR's low bandwidth per GB is a structural disadvantage here

segment: Power-capped or air-cooled sites (enterprise; telco and regional edge)
rationale: Many sites cannot host 130-230 kW liquid-cooled racks; a 150 W PCIe card fits standard servers, where NVL72's rack-scale lead does not apply; Intel targets the same niche with an air-cooled 160 GB LPDDR5X GPU
notes: Repo judgement; pool size not measured

segment: Agentic orchestration and AI head-node CPUs
qualcomm_public_asset: Dragonfly C1000; Oryon via NVLink Fusion
rationale: NVIDIA reports visibility to ~$20B of standalone CPU revenue this fiscal year within a '$200B' CPU opportunity; outside the GPU rack the CPU market is open (x86, Arm hyperscaler CPUs, Arm's own AGI CPU)
notes: C1000 deploys from H2 2028, so it meets the next generations of Vera and EPYC

rationale: Embedding-heavy ranking is capacity-bound and ran on LPDDR at Meta (MTIA v1/v2), but the biggest buyers build their own chips for it
notes: Buyer is often captive (MTIA); merchant opening is outside the top hyperscalers

segment: Small and medium dense models on cost per token
rationale: Dense models gain little from a 72-GPU NVLink domain; MI355X beat B200 on vLLM cost per token below 225 tokens/s per user, and depreciated H100s rent at ~$2.35/hr
notes: Commoditising pool: token prices for fixed capability fell ~286x in two years

rationale: Sovereign revenue exceeded ~$30B at NVIDIA in FY2026 and buyers such as HUMAIN multi-source (NVIDIA up to 600k GPUs, AMD 500 MW, Qualcomm 200 MW), but NVIDIA holds ~1.03M named sovereign GPUs
notes: Sovereign CUDA lock-in scored 3.75 of 5 in layer 09

segment: Edge-to-cloud continuity (hybrid on-device and cloud inference)
rationale: Qualcomm's edge chips sold ~$8.5B in one quarter vs ~$7.2B for NVIDIA's Edge platform, but no public evidence yet that device incumbency wins datacenter inference orders
notes: The pool for 'continuity' itself is unmeasured; scores are the repo's

qualcomm_public_asset: AWS custom inference silicon; Alphawave SerDes
rationale: The fastest-growing pool (Broadcom AI revenue $16.7B in one quarter, +221%); NVIDIA cannot stop a hyperscaler going custom and defends by co-option (NVLink Fusion in Trainium4); the rival here is Broadcom
notes: Lower margin per unit than merchant silicon; concentrated on a few buyers

rationale: Six or so buyers, all needing large scale-up domains and day-0 software; NVIDIA finishes runs fastest and TPUs are cheapest per FLOP
notes: Shown for reference; no Qualcomm product targets it
